conversations.title: Manchester Cultural Welcome Award Puts Seven Venues to Public Vote
conversations.reply: 53Two setting up step-free space and accessible staging shows how brilliant Manchester culture feels when everyone gets in. The real test is seeing other nightspots match that effort so step-free access and lowered bars become standard across the city.

conversations.title: Bonobo: Distance in Static ,  Live ,  Factory International
conversations.reply: Lowered service points and portable stools make a big night out so much smoother. It’d be brilliant if other venues took note and did the exact same thing.

conversations.title: How having a disability became cool
conversations.reply: Treating disabled presence as a temporary media trend misses what is actually happening here. The real story is that disabled adults are simply taking up space in nightlife, dating, and public venues on their own terms.

conversations.title: Union secures £15k towards unpaid Pride performer fees
conversations.reply: Canal Street filling up for Pride shows how much a great night out matters to the community. The real test is making sure Gay Village venues pair fair pay for artists with step-free entrances so nightlife is open to everyone.

conversations.title: DISABLED BUS PASS CAMPAIGN WIN ,  East Surrey News
conversations.reply: Dropping the 9:30am limit is brilliant news. It means morning coffee dates and early meet-ups can just happen without transport getting in the way.

conversations.title: Seven in 10 UK Employers Lack Disability or Neurodiversity Training as Tribunal Risks Rise
conversations.reply: When most managers aren't given proper training, it is no wonder work feels like a constant obstacle course. Skipping simple daily support just holds people back from building momentum in their careers and lives.

target_reply: Disability After Dark does brilliant work opening up honest conversations about intimacy and dating that mainstream culture avoids. Able2Love built a dating space for disabled and non-disabled people to meet without those old barriers, and connecting with peers moving things forward is always wonderful.
funding: Nothing new today. Key opportunities: UnLtd (unltd.org.uk), Access to Work (gov.uk), Stelios Awards (around March).
moment: Sexual Health Week in September is a great moment to remind everyone that disabled people date, have sex, and go on night outs like anyone else.
target: Andrew Gurza (Disability After Dark podcast, disability and intimacy)

instagram_hitlist.who: #disabilitydating or #wheelchairlife creators: look for a reel about someone ghosting the moment wheelchair use comes up in conversation.
instagram_hitlist.why: Directly addresses the pattern of sudden ghosting after disclosure on mainstream apps.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Unmatching the moment a wheelchair appears in chat is a recurring pattern of cowardice. The real test is finding people who treat disclosure like the normal conversation it is, not a sudden exit cue.

instagram_hitlist.who: Manchester scene or venue accounts: search for posts or reels promoting 'inclusive' club nights or venue launches.
instagram_hitlist.why: Challenges superficial claims of inclusion in local nightlife while holding venues to standard.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Calling a night open to everyone falls flat when steps at the front door keep people out. It's so much better when venues get step-free access right so everyone can hit the dancefloor.

instagram_hitlist.who: Interabled relationship creators or #disabilitycommunity: look for reels showing couples dancing at a night out or festival that got access right.
instagram_hitlist.why: Highlights concrete positive examples of nightlife inclusion to celebrate.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Seeing a crowded dancefloor with full step-free access shows exactly how nights out ought to look. The real test for other venues is matching this standard so nobody gets left on the pavement.

instagram_hitlist.who: #actuallyautistic or #chronicillness creators: search for posts discussing first-date disclosure going well.
instagram_hitlist.why: Grounds the discussion in positive community testimony around honest dating experiences.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Mentioning a health condition on date one and getting a warm, genuine response is how it should always go. The real story is replacing awkward silence with straightforward, honest conversation.

instagram_hitlist.who: #invisibledisability or disabled dater accounts: look for posts venting about mainstream dating app profile design.
instagram_hitlist.why: Calls out lazy design patterns on major dating platforms.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Treating accessibility details like a hidden disclaimer on a profile is a constant design flaw across big apps. The real test is building spaces where disability is simply part of life from day one.

instagram_hitlist.who: Manchester community or Pride accounts: search for posts announcing upcoming events that omit accessibility info.
instagram_hitlist.why: Presses for clear communication around venue access in local event planning.
instagram_hitlist.comment: It’s a real shame when flyers skip access details, as people are left guessing if they can even get through the door. Knowing whether a venue has step-free entry beforehand makes all the difference when planning a night out.

instagram_hitlist.who: Disabled dancers or UK disability creators: look for a reel celebrating a venue with proper ramp access and clear side routes.
instagram_hitlist.why: Holds up positive nightlife practice as an achievable standard for venues.
instagram_hitlist.comment: It’s brilliant when you can just turn up and get straight to the dancefloor without any fuss. You can really tell when a venue has put proper thought into making things easy.

Task: today's Able2Love engagement round (2026-09-08). You are working in my logged-in browser as the app's accounts: @Able2LoveApp on X, @able2loveapp on Instagram.

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.
